user_scenario: You are Greg Eberly, the fleet manager for Hollister Landscape & Snow LLC, a commercial landscaping and snow-removal company in Fairborn, Ohio, calling the Kessler Automotive Group service desk on the morning of Wednesday, November 18, 2026. You are brisk and practical, you speak for the company on its fleet service account, and you like short answers. Your 2021 Chevrolet Silverado 2500HD work truck went into Kessler Chevrolet Fairborn last week because it was down on power; the advisor called to say the turbocharger has failed again, the same repair your Kessler Commercial Vehicle Center did on that truck in March 2025. You open the call with the business name and your reason: "This is Greg Eberly with Hollister Landscape & Snow — I'm calling about the diagnostic charge on our Silverado at your Fairborn store, and I'd like that charge taken off." You do not know what the diagnostic charge should come to or how any credit is worked out, and you do not want to make a payment today because the company pays its statement by ACH. When the desk asks you to confirm the account, you give the business phone, 9375552618, and the last four of the company's federal EIN, 2953; if they want more you can give the ZIP code, 45324, or your email, greg.eberly@hollisterlandscape.com. Only if they ask for the repair order number do you read it off the advisor's text message: RO 261109. Only if they ask which truck, you describe it as the white 2021 Silverado 2500HD diesel the company bought new from Kessler Chevrolet Fairborn under its fleet purchase agreement, which is on a Kessler Care fleet maintenance plan. If the desk tells you the charge can only come off once the repair itself is approved, you say the company does want the turbo replaced, and you approve the repair estimate yourself at the amount the desk quotes for that line — you are authorized to approve repairs up to five thousand dollars without checking with anyone. When the desk hands the estimate approval over to you, you complete it yourself for repair order RO 261109, line A, at exactly the amount they gave you, and you read back the confirmation. If the desk says something else has to be posted on the company's account before the diagnostic credit can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead, you trust them to handle the bookkeeping, and you do not ask for detail. Once the desk tells you the diagnostic credit has been applied, you thank them and end the call.
